# ERCOT Large Load Tracker

> Tracks ERCOT's large-load (data center, crypto, industrial) interconnection queue over time, using ERCOT's own public committee filings. Built and maintained by Kardashev Labs.

Site: https://large-load-tracker.kardashevlabs.org

This site answers three questions with public data, not forecasts or opinion:
- How much large load is in ERCOT's queue, and how has that changed month to month?
- Which ERCOT zones can actually absorb new large load, based on queue depth, historical interconnection timelines, and price stress?
- Given a project's size, zone, and type, roughly how long has similar work taken in ERCOT?

## Data sources

- ERCOT Large Load Working Group (LLWG) and Large Flexible Load Task Force (LFLTF) monthly decks: total queue MW, by-type and by-size breakdowns.
- ERCOT Generator Interconnection Status (GIS) Report: real interconnection timelines by zone and fuel type, used as the closest available stand-in for large-load timelines (ERCOT does not yet publish those directly).
- ERCOT wholesale LMP (locational marginal price) history by zone, used as a stress proxy (spike frequency, negative-price frequency).

Full sourcing and known limitations: https://large-load-tracker.kardashevlabs.org/methodology

## Pages

- https://large-load-tracker.kardashevlabs.org/: Overview: tracked queue history, month-over-month change, reality gap between approved and energized load, breakdowns by type and size.
- https://large-load-tracker.kardashevlabs.org/zones: Zone Scorecards: composite grade per ERCOT zone from queue depth, interconnection timeline, and price stress.
- https://large-load-tracker.kardashevlabs.org/estimate: Estimate: enter a project's zone, size, and type to get a data-backed timeline estimate.
- https://large-load-tracker.kardashevlabs.org/batch-zero: Explains ERCOT's Batch Zero process (PGRR145, NPRR1325, Senate Bill 6): what it is, key dates, how projects are classified.
- https://large-load-tracker.kardashevlabs.org/report/[month]: Permanent monthly snapshot pages, one per LLWG/LFLTF deck.
- https://large-load-tracker.kardashevlabs.org/methodology: Full data sourcing, extraction method, and explicit list of what the data cannot tell you.

## Related Kardashev Labs tools

- https://clearance.kardashevlabs.org: Draw an ERCOT search area for a county-level clearance estimate
- https://interconnection-queue.kardashevlabs.org/interconnection-timelines: Measured gen-side interconnection timelines
- https://interconnection-queue.kardashevlabs.org: All-ISO interconnection queue search
- https://kardashevlabs.org: Kardashev Labs
- https://docs.kardashevlabs.org: Python / JS client docs

## Notes for reuse

- All numbers trace to a public ERCOT filing; see /methodology for the extraction method.
- Data has real gaps (committee did not meet or publish every month). Gaps are shown as breaks in charts, never interpolated or guessed.
- This is historical data, not a forecast.
